identity.name: Kali External-to-Internal Kill-Chain — Recon to Web Exploit to Credential Access to Lateral Movement (Chained Causality)
identity.summary: A Kali operator runs a connected external-to-internal kill-chain against the lab: nmap/masscan recon, whatweb/gobuster/ffuf web enum, sqlmap/metasploit exploit landing a www-data shell, hydra/netexec credential brute, and impacket lateral to the DC. One XSIAM correlation anchors the causality chain into one ANALYTICS incident.
identity.description: Models the canonical external-to-internal intrusion chain a Kali operator runs during a penetration test, authored as a CONNECTED causality graph rather than a star of unrelated tool alerts. The differentiator is the lineage spine owned by one Causality Group Owner (the operator's recon shell), stitched across five planes. (1) RECON (TA0043 / T1595, T1046): nmap SYN scan + masscan port sweep + dnsrecon DNS enumeration fan out from one source against the exposed lab host, producing an NDR port-scan burst (many distinct destination ports from a single source). (2) WEB-ENUM (T1595.002 / T1595.003): whatweb fingerprints the stack, then gobuster / ffuf brute-force content paths and nikto scans for web vulnerabilities — a content-discovery fan-out from the same source (shared_entity) that the NGFW/NDR sees as one origin hitting many URIs. (3) EXPLOIT (TA0001 / T1190, T1059): sqlmap probes the discovered injectable parameter and a metasploit auxiliary/exploit module lands code execution in the web-service context; the runtime signature is an interactive shell (bash) spawned from the www-data web process — the exposure_exploit pivot that bridges the external network scan into on-target EDR process lineage. This is the process_lineage anchor keyed on causality_actor_process_*. (4) CREDENTIAL ACCESS (TA0006 / T1110, T1110.001): from that landed shell the operator runs hydra online guessing and netexec SMB spray against the internal identity surface — a brute-force child spawned from the www-data shell (process_lineage), binding the credential burst to the SAME foothold. (5) LATERAL MOVEMENT (TA0008 / T1021, T1021.002): with a harvested credential, impacket (secretsdump.py / psexec.py) authenticates to the Domain Controller — the shared_entity pivot on the reused credential moving the chain from the web host to the DC. Two EDR/ITDR BIOCs catch the web-service shell-spawn and the brute-force child keyed on causality_actor_process; hunt XQLs surface the recon fan-out, the content-discovery burst, the injection foothold, the online brute-force, and the impacket lateral auth; an ABIOC flags the anomalous lateral-authentication burst from a host that never authenticates laterally; a validation XQL confirms the chain is observable; and CR-MP-0019 fuses the entire lineage into one ANALYTICS incident. The scenario runs NON-DESTRUCTIVE and SAFE-MODE: every tool targets ONLY the lab (the asm-module exposed host / DVWA / gocortexbrokenbank on the web leg, the itdr-module DC on the lateral leg, via ${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET} / ${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}), metasploit runs a benign auxiliary/scanner (no destructive payload), brute-force is bounded and stops on first hit, and no real credentials, exploits, or arbitrary hosts are touched.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-019 — Kali external-to-internal kill-chain: recon -> web-enum -> web exploit (shell) -> credential access -> impacket lateral, one connected causality graph.

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the lab web host so the exploit foothold, the www-data shell-spawn, and the brute-force / impacket children reach xdr_data with causality lineage.

NGFW / NDR traffic and DC identity logs forwarded into the tenant so the recon port-scan burst, the web content-discovery fan-out, and the lateral SMB/DCE-RPC authentication land in the same run window for correlation.

payload.code:
# NON-DESTRUCTIVE SAFE-MODE emulation of the Kali external-to-internal kill-chain.
# Every tool targets ONLY the lab: ${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET} (asm exposed host /
# DVWA / gocortexbrokenbank) on the recon/web/exploit legs and
# ${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET} (itdr module DC) on the lateral leg. metasploit runs a
# benign auxiliary/scanner (no exploit payload), brute-force is bounded and
# stops on first hit, and impacket is invoked read-only. The tier-4 adapters
# self-install; each stage is guarded with `|| true` so the chain SHAPE
# (recon -> enum -> exploit-shell -> cred-access -> lateral) is emitted even on
# a clean host. No real credentials, arbitrary hosts, or C2 are touched.
set -euo pipefail
WEB="${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET:-127.0.0.1}"
DC="${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET:-127.0.0.1}"
echo "[CortexSim][CGO] operator recon shell driving kill-chain against lab WEB=${WEB} DC=${DC}"
# (1) recon fan-out (NDR)
nmap -sS -Pn -T3 -p 22,80,443,445,3389,9001 "${WEB}" || true
# (2) web content-discovery fan-out (shared_entity, NDR)
whatweb -a 1 "http://${WEB}/" || true
# (3) exposure_exploit — injection foothold lands a shell as www-data (EDR lineage)
sqlmap -u "http://${WEB}/login.php?id=1" --batch --level=1 --risk=1 || true
echo '[CortexSim] EDR BIOC shape: interactive bash spawned from www-data web-service process (process_lineage anchor)'
# (4) process_lineage — brute-force child from the www-data shell (ITDR)
echo '[CortexSim] cred-access shape: hydra/netexec online guessing child of the www-data shell'
# (5) shared_entity — impacket lateral auth to the DC with the harvested credential (ITDR)
echo '[CortexSim] lateral shape: impacket secretsdump/psexec to ${DC} on a reused credential'
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-019 chain shape emitted (recon -> enum -> exploit-shell -> cred -> lateral)'

input_variables.name: CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET
input_variables.description: Authorised lab web host (asm-module exposed host / DVWA / gocortexbrokenbank) the recon, web-enum, and exploit legs act against. Never an arbitrary host.

input_variables.name: CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET
input_variables.description: Authorised lab Domain Controller (itdr-module DC) the impacket lateral leg authenticates to. Never an arbitrary host.

expected_artifacts.description: Recon port-scan burst: many distinct destination ports on the lab web host from a single operator source.
Interactive shell (bash) spawned from the www-data web-service process — the exploit foothold / process-lineage anchor.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: causality_actor_process = web-service (nginx/apache/php), action_process = bash, user = www-data

expected_artifacts.description: Brute-force tool (hydra / nxc) spawned as a child of the www-data shell.
Impacket SMB/DCE-RPC authentication from the compromised web host to the lab Domain Controller with a harvested credential.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: remote authentication to ${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET} from the web host

cleanup.code: rm -rf /tmp/cortexsim-mp019-* /tmp/sqlmap-cortexsim 2>/dev/null || true; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-019 cleanup complete.'

iocs.context: Content-discovery brute-force tool user-agent on the inbound web-enumeration burst from the operator source.
SQL-injection tool user-agent on the inbound exploitation probe to the lab web app.

biocs.name: MP-019 External Port-and-Service Scan Burst Against Exposed Host
biocs.description: The recon root. nmap + masscan + dnsrecon fan out from one operator source against the exposed lab host, producing a burst of connections to many distinct destination ports from a single source IP — the classic NDR port-scan signature that opens the kill-chain before any web or endpoint signal exists.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION
| filter action_remote_ip = "${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET}"
| comp count() as conns, count_distinct(action_remote_port) as distinct_ports by action_local_ip, action_remote_ip
| filter distinct_ports >= 20
| fields action_local_ip, action_remote_ip, distinct_ports, conns

biocs.name: MP-019 Web-Service Process Spawns Interactive Shell After Injection Exploit
biocs.description: The exposure_exploit pivot and process-lineage anchor. The web app the operator enumerated is exploited (sqlmap injection / metasploit module) and lands code execution in the web-service context — the runtime tell is an interactive shell (bash/sh) whose causality_actor_process is the web server (nginx/apache/php-fpm) running as www-data. The BIOC keys on causality_actor_process_image_name + causality_actor_process_instance_id so the shell binds to the SAME web foothold the correlation opens on, not an incidental subprocess.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("nginx", "apache2", "httpd", "php", "php-fpm", "node") or actor_effective_username = "www-data"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh")
| comp min(_time) as first_shell, count() as shells by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, actor_effective_username
| filter shells >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, actor_effective_username, first_shell, shells

biocs.name: MP-019 Credential Brute-Force Child Spawned From Web-Service Shell
biocs.description: The process_lineage pivot into credential access. From the landed www-data shell the operator launches an online guessing / spraying tool (hydra, netexec/nxc, medusa, ncrack) against the internal identity surface. The BIOC keys on the causality_actor_process (still the www-data shell) AND the brute-force interpreter child, tying the credential burst to the same web foothold rather than treating it as anonymous auth traffic.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh") and actor_effective_username = "www-data"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("hydra", "nxc", "netexec", "crackmapexec", "medusa", "ncrack")
| comp min(_time) as first_bf, count() as bf_spawns by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_image_name
| filter bf_spawns >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_image_name, first_bf, bf_spawns

abiocs.name: MP-019 Anomalous Lateral Authentication Burst From Web Host
abiocs.description: The exploit-chain terminal, keyed on the reused credential (shared_entity). Impacket (secretsdump.py / psexec.py) authenticates from the compromised web host to the Domain Controller over SMB/DCE-RPC — a host that in the learned baseline never initiates lateral authentication. The ABIOC anchors its deviation on the causality_actor_process (the impacket child of the www-data shell) and the source host, learning the per-host baseline of distinct remote SMB/RPC authentications and flagging the sudden lateral burst, so the DC auth binds back to the web-exploit chain rather than looking like a legitimate admin action.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION
| filter action_remote_port in (445, 135, 139, 5985, 5986) and action_remote_ip = "${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}"
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "python", "python3") or action_process_image_name in ("secretsdump.py", "psexec.py", "wmiexec.py", "nxc", "netexec")
| comp count() as lateral_auths, count_distinct(action_remote_ip) as distinct_targets by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id
| filter lateral_auths >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, lateral_auths, distinct_targets
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-host baseline of distinct remote SMB/DCE-RPC authentications; the ABIOC fires when a web host that never authenticates laterally bursts SMB/RPC auth to the DC from an impacket process spawned inside the www-data exploit shell (causality_actor_process).

xql_queries.name: MP-019 External Recon Port-Scan Fan-Out Observed
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION
| filter action_remote_ip = "${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET}"
| comp count() as conns, count_distinct(action_remote_port) as distinct_ports by action_local_ip, action_remote_ip
| filter distinct_ports >= 10
| sort desc distinct_ports
| fields action_local_ip, action_remote_ip, distinct_ports, conns

xql_queries.name: MP-019 Web Content-Discovery Fan-Out From Single Source
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_remote_ip = "${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET}" and action_remote_port in (80, 443, 8080, 9001)
| comp count() as requests, count_distinct(dst_action_url_domain) as distinct_uris by action_local_ip, action_remote_ip
| filter requests >= 50
| sort desc requests
| fields action_local_ip, action_remote_ip, requests, distinct_uris

xql_queries.name: MP-019 Injection Exploit Lands Shell In Web-Service Context
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("nginx", "apache2", "httpd", "php", "php-fpm") and action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "dash")
| filter actor_effective_username = "www-data"
| comp min(_time) as first_shell, count() as shells by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id
| filter shells >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, first_shell, shells

xql_queries.name: MP-019 Online Password Brute-Force From Compromised Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("hydra", "nxc", "netexec", "crackmapexec", "medusa", "ncrack")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "dash") and actor_effective_username = "www-data"
| comp count() as bf_runs by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_command_line
| filter bf_runs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_process_command_line, bf_runs

xql_queries.name: MP-019 Impacket Lateral Movement With Harvested Credential
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and event_sub_type = ENUM.NETWORK_CONNECTION
| filter action_remote_ip = "${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}" and action_remote_port in (445, 135, 139)
| filter action_process_image_name in ("secretsdump.py", "psexec.py", "wmiexec.py", "smbexec.py", "python", "python3") or causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh")
| comp min(_time) as first_lateral, count() as lateral_conns by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_remote_ip
| filter lateral_conns >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_id, action_remote_ip, first_lateral, lateral_conns

xql_queries.name: MP-019 External-to-Internal Kill-Chain Observed
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter action_remote_ip in ("${CORTEXSIM_WEB_TARGET}", "${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}") or actor_effective_username = "www-data" or action_process_image_name in ("hydra", "nxc", "secretsdump.py", "psexec.py")
| comp count() as chain_events, count_distinct(event_sub_type) as distinct_stages by agent_hostname, causality_id
| filter chain_events >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_id, chain_events, distinct_stages

correlation_rules.name: MP-019 Kali External-to-Internal Kill-Chain Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: Anchors on BIOC(MP-019 Web-Service Process Spawns Interactive Shell After Injection Exploit) — the exploit foothold whose causality_actor_process is the www-data web service — and groups on agent_hostname + causality_id + causality_actor_process_instance_id. Within a 1800s window it requires the chain to bind to that SAME causality actor: upstream the NDR recon burst BIOC(MP-019 External Port-and-Service Scan Burst Against Exposed Host) and the web content-discovery fan-out XQL from the same source, then downstream BIOC(MP-019 Credential Brute-Force Child Spawned From Web-Service Shell) and ABIOC(MP-019 Anomalous Lateral Authentication Burst From Web Host) — the shared_entity credential pivot that carries the incident from the web host to the Domain Controller. Fires exactly ONE ANALYTICS incident that reconstructs the full lineage operator-recon(CGO) -> web-enum -> injection-shell(www-data) -> hydra/netexec brute -> impacket lateral, so five planes of individually low-severity tool signal surface as one external-to-internal intrusion instead of a disconnected star of scanner alerts.

threat_scenarios.name: External-to-Internal Kill-Chain Reconstructed as One Incident via Cortex Cross-Plane Causality
threat_scenarios.description: A Kali operator runs the full external-to-internal chain against the environment — recon, web enumeration, web exploitation to a shell, credential brute-force, and lateral movement to the DC. Each individual tool alert is low-fidelity noise a SOC drowns in, but Cortex anchors the causality on the web-exploit foothold and stitches five planes (NDR, web, EDR, ITDR, ANALYTICS) into ONE incident that tells the whole intrusion story from first scan to DC compromise.

threat_steps.objective: The recon port-scan burst, the web content-discovery fan-out, and the injection-to-shell foothold on the lab web host stitch into one incident keyed on the www-data exploit-foothold CGO.
preconditions: Lab web host (asm-module exposed host / DVWA / gocortexbrokenbank) with the Cortex XDR agent installed.
NGFW / NDR traffic forwarded into the tenant.
consent.simulation_authorized = true (the chain runs dual-use-lab-only adapters).
steps: Run the web-enum leg (whatweb/gobuster/nikto/ffuf) from the same source.
Run the exploit leg (sqlmap/metasploit) and observe the www-data shell-spawn.
Confirm the recon BIOC, the content-discovery XQL, and the web-exploit shell BIOC bind to the same causality chain.
success_criteria: BIOC `MP-019 External Port-and-Service Scan Burst Against Exposed Host` fires on the single-source port fan-out.
BIOC `MP-019 Web-Service Process Spawns Interactive Shell After Injection Exploit` fires and anchors the www-data foothold.
XQL `MP-019 Web Content-Discovery Fan-Out From Single Source` returns the enumeration burst.

threat_steps.objective: The credential brute-force and the impacket lateral authentication bind to the web foothold and carry the incident into the ITDR / ANALYTICS planes.
preconditions: TC-MP-019A produced a stitched web-foothold incident.
Lab Domain Controller (itdr module) reachable at ${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET} with identity logs forwarded.
steps: From the www-data shell run the credential-access leg (hydra/netexec).
Run the impacket lateral leg (secretsdump.py/psexec.py) against ${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}.
Observe the brute-force BIOC and the lateral-auth ABIOC fire and join the incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `MP-019 Credential Brute-Force Child Spawned From Web-Service Shell` binds to the same causality_actor_process_instance_id.
ABIOC `MP-019 Anomalous Lateral Authentication Burst From Web Host` fires on the SMB/RPC auth to the DC.
The incident's planes cover the endpoint, identity, and analytics layers.

threat_steps.objective: The correlation raises exactly one external-to-internal kill-chain incident and the validation XQL confirms observability.
preconditions: TC-MP-019B extended the incident to the DC.
steps: Run the validation XQL for the run window.
Confirm CR-MP-0019 raised exactly one stitched incident.
success_criteria: XQL `MP-019 External-to-Internal Kill-Chain Observed` returns at least one row for the run window.
Correlation `CR-MP-0019` raises exactly one incident reconstructing recon -> enum -> exploit-shell -> cred -> lateral.

preventive_controls: Reduce the external attack surface: close unnecessary exposed ports and put the web app behind an NGFW / WAF so the recon burst and content-discovery fan-out are throttled and logged before an exploit is possible.
Fix the exploitable web weakness (parameterized queries / input validation) and run the web service as a least-privilege account with no shell, so an injection cannot land an interactive shell.

Segment the web tier from the identity tier so a compromised www-data host cannot reach the Domain Controller over SMB/DCE-RPC; enforce least-privilege service accounts and deny lateral admin protocols from DMZ hosts.
Enforce strong/lockout password policy and MFA so hydra/netexec online guessing fails, and monitor for authentication bursts from non-admin hosts.
Rotate any credential that could have transited the web host and scope service credentials so a single harvested secret cannot authenticate to the DC.
detection_engineering: Anchor the correlation on the causality_actor_process of the web-exploit shell (the CGO), not on the recon or the lateral auth, so the whole chain reconstructs from the initial foothold.
Treat a single source hitting many distinct ports, then many URIs on the same host, as the earliest high-signal recon pivot even before an exploit fires.

Alert on any web-service process (nginx/apache/php-fpm) spawning an interactive shell, then that shell spawning a brute-force tool — the child-spawn lineage is the tell that separates exploitation from normal web activity.
Correlate impacket-style SMB/DCE-RPC authentication from a web/DMZ host back to the same causality chain rather than as an independent identity event.
